newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon magistrate wants waste importers jailed.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon magistrate wants waste importers jailed.

text.p: A Lebanese investigating magistrate demanded on Thursday five to 10 years imprisonment for three Lebanese charged with importing 680 tonnes of German plastic toxic waste in 1996, judicial sources said.

They said magistrate Saeed Mirza charged John Zakhia Beayno, his brother Efram and Michael Salim Andraous with illegally importing the 36 containers of "polluted plastic waste and toxic chemicals that endanger public health".

John Beayno, who is in custody, told prosecutors that his brother Efram who lives in Russia brokered the deal with a Jordanian businessman in Germany. Andraous, an agent for the Jordanian businessman at Beirut port, was released on bail after initial investigations.
The shipment has been held at the port since August and negotiations are under way with Germany to take it back.
The international environmental organisation Greenpeace said earlier the shipment included a mixture of plastic wastes contaminated with laboratory chemicals, pesticides and chemical fertilisers.
